newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission may need to study U.S. plane merger.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission may need to study U.S. plane merger.

text.p: The European Commission has not yet been informed about the merger of U.S. plane makers Boeing and McDonnel Douglas and it is not clear whether it will have to probe the deal, a Commission source said on Monday.
"We don't know yet...we have not been informed," he said, adding that it depended on the presence of the companies on the European market. "It is all a matter of turnover figures."
Under EU rules, the Commission studies corporate deals to see whether they may harm competition in the 15-nation bloc if they meet certain turnover thresholds.

For the Commission to study the case, the combined worldwide turnover must be at least five billion European currency units ($6.25 billion) and each of the companies must have a turnover of 250 million Ecus in the EU.
Most deals are cleared after a one-month routine inquiry.
